exam.title: CompTIA Cloud+ (V4)
exam.study_prerequisites: CompTIA recommends 2–3 years in systems administration or networking plus 12 months of hands-on cloud experience. Practice provider-neutral requirement mapping, availability/network/compute/storage/database/cost architecture, migrations and IaC, scaling/backup/observability, IAM/data/network/container security and compliance evidence, CI/CD and event-driven integration, and layered troubleshooting across at least one cloud with translation to a second provider.

review.notes: All six weighted V4 domains are mapped to requirements, selection, IaC deployment, observable operations, layered security, DevOps delivery and systematic troubleshooting, with three scenarios, eight safe multi-provider labs and 42 original checks. The estimated-2027 statement is explicitly not an exact retirement date. All nine guide URLs are cataloged; source health is recorded separately. No proprietary objectives, PBQs, course labs or recalled items are used.

findings.title: Experience advice added an unsupported extra year
findings.evidence: Current page recommends 2–3 years as systems administrator or cloud engineer; PDF adds equivalent Network+/Server+ knowledge, without an extra 12-month requirement.
findings.recommendation: Correct both guide and exam catalog and distinguish recommendations from mandatory prerequisites.
findings.resolution: Correct both guide and exam catalog and distinguish recommendations from mandatory prerequisites.

findings.title: The summary omitted explicit detailed scope
findings.evidence: PDF objective 1.11 includes AI/ML and IoT; 2.1 includes community cloud, and 5.3/5.4 enumerate integration styles and tools.
findings.recommendation: Map all 33 numbered objectives and add original capability/evaluation, deployment-model and integration-role teaching.
findings.resolution: Map all 33 numbered objectives and add original capability/evaluation, deployment-model and integration-role teaching.

findings.title: PDF expands CLI incorrectly for this management context
findings.evidence: The outline prints Common Language Infrastructure in cloud-management access; the provider interface documentation explicitly names Command Line Interface.
findings.recommendation: Teach the correct management-interface meaning while identifying the outline wording, without introducing unrelated .NET execution semantics.
findings.resolution: Teach the correct management-interface meaning while identifying the outline wording, without introducing unrelated .NET execution semantics.

findings.title: Secret-free state is not guaranteed by output redaction
findings.evidence: Sensitive flags can hide normal display while state and saved plan files still contain values; ephemeral/write-only capabilities have constraints.
findings.recommendation: Replace blanket keep-secrets-out-of-state wording with artifact protection and version/context/provider-aware guidance.
findings.resolution: Replace blanket keep-secrets-out-of-state wording with artifact protection and version/context/provider-aware guidance.

findings.title: A successful change plan has a nonzero detailed code
findings.evidence: The documented detailed exit codes are zero unchanged, one error and two changes present.
findings.recommendation: Teach automation interpretation and execute unchanged/update/replacement/invalid-input cases using only local terraform_data.
findings.resolution: Teach automation interpretation and execute unchanged/update/replacement/invalid-input cases using only local terraform_data.

findings.title: Cost notification is delayed rather than an instantaneous cap
findings.evidence: AWS documents billing/notification delay and possible further charges before or after an alert.
findings.recommendation: Explain budget signals versus enforced controls with invented cost/capacity examples and no vendor price or spend-cap guarantee.
findings.resolution: Explain budget signals versus enforced controls with invented cost/capacity examples and no vendor price or spend-cap guarantee.

findings.title: Delivery retries need explicit effect handling
findings.evidence: A standard queue can deliver another copy; consumer idempotence must be designed rather than inferred from acknowledgement.
findings.recommendation: Add an original locally executed receipt/effect transaction and explain external-action, acknowledgement and retention limits.
findings.resolution: Add an original locally executed receipt/effect transaction and explain external-action, acknowledgement and retention limits.

findings.title: Response codes are discriminating evidence, not a diagnosis
findings.evidence: RFC 9110 distinguishes authentication, refusal/non-disclosure and gateway/upstream status meanings.
findings.recommendation: Add a qualified HTTP investigation table and preserve host/certificate context during alternate-address tests.
findings.resolution: Add a qualified HTTP investigation table and preserve host/certificate context during alternate-address tests.

local_validation.execution_boundary: Terraform built-in terraform_data and SQLite acted only on synthetic local state/databases in an owned temporary workspace. No external Terraform provider, cloud API, credentials, queue, remote message, workload deployment or billed resource used. Temporary fixtures cleaned.
limits: Terraform lifecycle is real but its resource represents local state only; no actual cloud replicas, image pulls, policy enforcement, provider drift or availability test.
SQLite tests cover transaction rollback, reconnect, an owned worker exit before commit and concurrent connections; not arbitrary storage/power-loss durability or distributed exactly-once processing.
Receipt deduplication has no expiry/retention cleanup; no external side effect or queue acknowledgement is atomic with this local transaction.
Availability, capacity, throughput, recovery, retries and cost are invented arithmetic models, not measured performance, vendor SLAs or prices.
All eight complete cloud labs remain proposed.

limitations: Same-context AI review; independent human review pending.

No external Terraform provider, cloud API/credentials, queue, remote message, image pull, billed resource, workload rollout, live backup/failover or full cloud lab executed. All eight complete labs remain proposed.
SQLite checks cover rollback, reconnect, an owned worker exit before commit and concurrent connections; no arbitrary storage corruption/power-loss or distributed exactly-once guarantee.
Local receipts have no expiry cleanup or production authentication; external side effects/queue acknowledgement are outside the database transaction.
Availability, failover capacity, queue drain, throughput, RTO/RPO, retry and cost examples are invented models, not measured performance, current prices or vendor SLAs.
OReilly and Udemy blocked automated catalog rechecking; earlier edition/page/runtime/instructor/date/assessment claims remain unverified. Paid interiors and banks unreviewed.
Retirement remains estimated 2027 without an exact date; public document 5.0 is not a replacement exam announcement.
